name: Nivolumab Monotherapy (CheckMate-141), Platinum-Refractory Recurrent or Metastatic Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
disease: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (non-nasopharyngeal)

biomarkers.PD_L1: not required for eligibility; greater overall survival benefit observed when PD-L1 expression level is at least 1%
biomarkers.note: Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers v2.2026 Discussion MS-59, the OS benefit with nivolumab appeared confined to patients with PD-L1 expression at least 1% (8.7 vs 4.6 months), with no OS advantage demonstrated below 1%; nivolumab is listed as a subsequent-line option (SYST-A 4 of 7) without a mandatory PD-L1 threshold for use. PD-L1 testing informs expected benefit but is not an eligibility gate here.

lineOfTherapy: second-line or later (platinum-refractory: disease progression on or after platinum-based therapy)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: disease progression on or after platinum-based therapy
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, SYST-A 4 of 7 (Recurrent, Unresectable, or Metastatic Disease, Subsequent-Line: Nivolumab if disease progression on or after platinum therapy, category 1)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: recurrent, unresectable, or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma with no surgical or radiotherapy option
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: non-nasopharyngeal primary; nasopharynx follows a separate systemic-therapy pathway (NASO-B)
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, SYST-A 1 of 7 (Principles of Systemic Therapy for Non-Nasopharyngeal Cancers header)

drugs.name: Nivolumab

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
provenance.locator: Discussion MS-59 (two FDA-approved dosing regimens for nivolumab for SCCHN: 240 mg every 2 weeks or 480 mg every 4 weeks); indication SYST-A 4 of 7 (subsequent-line, post-platinum, category 1)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, Discussion MS-59. Nivolumab 240 mg IV flat dose on day 1 every 14 days. Source-stated alternate schedule: 480 mg IV every 28 days. Flat milligram dosing (basis flat); source states flat mg, not mg/kg. Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. A nivolumab and hyaluronidase-nvhy subcutaneous formulation may be substituted with different dosing/administration (SYST-A 1 of 7); not encoded here.

regimen.cycles: until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; alternate schedule 480 mg every 28 days
supportiveCare: Immune-related adverse event surveillance for nivolumab (thyroid, hepatic, pulmonary, colitis, dermatologic, endocrine).
Antiemetic prophylaxis not routinely required for single-agent checkpoint inhibitor (minimal emetic risk).

monitoring: immune-related toxicity screen (TSH/free T4, LFTs, glucose, cortisol as indicated) during nivolumab
imaging every 2 to 3 cycles in the recurrent/metastatic setting (Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, SYST-A 1 of 7 general principles)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold nivolumab and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; obtain clinical review before rechallenge.

core.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22nd ed.
core.locator: Head and Neck Cancer chapter (lines 88276 to 88285): a randomized trial of the PD-1 inhibitor nivolumab versus chemotherapy in second-line recurrent or metastatic disease showed increased 1-year survival with fewer severe treatment-related toxicities

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
guideline.locator: SYST-A 4 of 7 (Recurrent, Unresectable, or Metastatic Disease, Subsequent-Line: Nivolumab if progression on or after platinum, category 1); dosing Discussion MS-59 (CheckMate-141 dosing narrative)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for nivolumab monotherapy (CheckMate-141) in platinum-refractory recurrent or metastatic non-nasopharyngeal head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Serves the squamous-cell head and neck sites (reference sites #32 to 39 and #41), not nasopharynx (separate NASO-B pathway) and not salivary gland (#40, separate protocol). Nivolumab flat 240 mg IV every 14 days (alternate 480 mg every 28 days) is sourced to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026 Discussion MS-59, which states the two FDA-approved SCCHN dosing regimens as flat milligram doses (basis flat), not mg/kg. The subsequent-line, post-platinum indication (category 1) is from SYST-A 4 of 7. PD-L1 is captured as a benefit modifier, not an eligibility gate, per the Discussion (MS-59). Setting recurrent/metastatic, palliative intent, second-line or later. No numeric field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
